sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Srivastava,Ramesh Chand Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.
2. Present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.605 of 2022, under Sections 376, 328, 120-B of IPC, Police Station Narkhi, District Firozabad.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that initially, the FIR was lodged under Section 363 of IPC and during investigation, Sections 376, 328, 120-B were added.

The applicant is not named in the FIR and his name is surfaced in the statement of the informant, when he was interrogated third time after recording the statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr PC.

In the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr PC, the victim has even not named the Ramu Alias Ram Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107991217/
1 applicant and she has specifically stated the she had gone to the house of her friend.

sentences.text: The victim was medically examined and no external or internal injury is found.
The applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has an apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.
4. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail.

5. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98, the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either way, which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
8. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have a liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.
9. It is made clear that the observations made herein-above shall not, in any way, affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
